title: Adaptive mini-batching and kernel scheduler to reduce short-embed tail spikes
creator: Anika Rao
description:
Problem: We continue to see p95/p99 latency spikes on the embeddings endpoint for workloads dominated by a high volume of short requests (<= 64 tokens). Existing continuous-batching helps throughput but introduces head-of-line and kernel cold overhead for very small microbatches. Goal: reduce p95/p99 by 30-50% for short-embed traffic while keeping per-token cost within 10% of current baselines.

Proposed approach:
- Implement an adaptive mini-batching layer in the inference gateway that coalesces requests across a short time window (configurable down to 200us) and groups by model/quantization path.
- Add a lightweight scheduler in the runtime to select execution kernels based on microbatch size and sequence length distribution (fast-path kernels for tiny batches, fallback kernels for larger ones).
- Introduce a tiny-per-request cold-start cache to avoid repeated kernel init on ephemeral microbatches.
- Augment telemetry: per-request batch size tag, kernel-path used, queue-wait time, per-request latency breakdown.

Deliverables:
1) Design doc with simulation results for different coalescing windows and throughput-latency tradeoffs.
2) Prototype gateway coalescer + runtime scheduler A/B on a staging fleet.
3) Load test report showing p50/p95/p99 improvements and cost delta.
4) Rollout plan (canary by customer tier, circuit-breaker thresholds).

Success criteria:
- p95 for short-embed workloads reduced by >= 30% in canary compared to baseline.
- p99 reduced by >= 20% with no increase in error rate or tail token generation anomalies.
- Unit cost per 1k tokens increases <= 10% or decreases.

Risks & mitigations:
- Coalescing window increases latency for single-request workloads: mitigate with dynamic window based on request SLAs and client header hints.
- Kernel-selection mistakes could regress quality on quantized paths: include validation set checks and automatic rollback.
- Cross-customer coalescing sensitivities: ensure tenant affinity and privacy-safe coalescing policies.
